syllabus.quote: Compare identify/comment on similarities and/or differences

one_line: For Compare, give similarities and differences. For Contrast, give differences only, and write every point about both things.

points.heading: Which sides to give
points.text: Mark schemes for Compare list similarities and differences, with one mark for each valid point. Some mark schemes need at least one similarity and one difference for full marks. June 2022 Paper 12 is one example.

cites.quote: Must have at least one similarity and one difference to gain full marks

points.heading: Which sides to give
points.text: Some mark schemes cap each side. A 5-mark question can allow at most 4 marks for similarities and 4 for differences. An answer with one side only cannot reach full marks.

points.heading: Which sides to give
points.text: Give similarities and differences in a Compare answer, even when the question does not ask for both. The examiner reports differ here. The March 2023 report advised both sides in every case. The November 2022 report gave full marks for one side on one question. An answer with both sides is safe under either view.

cites.quote: even if it does not, candidates are advised to give both to ensure access to the full mark range.
However, in this case, full marks could have been achieved with only similarities or only differences in the answers.

points.heading: Which sides to give
points.text: Students often leave out the similarities. The November 2025 examiner report on Paper 11 said that few, if any, candidates gave them.

cites.quote: Few, if any, candidates identified similarities between the two methods.

points.heading: Which sides to give
points.text: Contrast means differences only. Similarities in a Contrast answer get no marks and use up your time.

cites.quote: Any references to similarities were ignored and not given credit because these did not answer the question.

points.heading: Write each point as a comparison
points.text: Make each point say something about both things. 'A LAN covers a small area' gets no mark. 'A LAN covers a smaller area than a WAN' gets a mark. The June 2025 report on a Contrast question said you need not write out both sides every time. The point must still read as a comparison.

cites.quote: For example, ‘a LAN covers a small geographical area’ on its own is a true fact but does not answer the question. However, ‘a LAN covers a smaller geographical area than a WAN’ answers the question and would gain credit.
whilst candidates do have to show some awareness that they are comparing, there is no requirement for candidates to present both sides of the argument.

points.heading: Write each point as a comparison
points.text: Write each difference as one sentence about both things, joined by 'whereas'. Do not write one paragraph about A and then another paragraph about B. Examiners gave no marks when they could not see the comparison.

cites.quote: differences are best presented together, perhaps joined by the use of ‘whereas’. In some cases, candidates wrote two separate descriptions one of phishing and the other of vishing.
this clarity was sometimes lacking and so marks were not awarded.

points.heading: Write each point as a comparison
points.text: Bullet lists and tables are risky in a comparison. The June 2023 examiner report says lists of points, bulleted or in tables, are unlikely to get full marks. Write each comparison as a sentence.

cites.quote: candidates who provide lists of points, bulleted or in tables, are unlikely to gain full marks because the question asks for comparisons which are best written in free response.

points.heading: Compare the two named things
points.text: Do not repeat the question as a similarity. If the question says both devices exchange data, 'both exchange data' gets no mark. The examiners also called very general similarities weak, such as 'both are plastic cards'.

cites.quote: answers that repeat the question, in this case stating that both exchange data in networks, will not be given credit.
Weaker answers referred to both being plastic cards

points.heading: Compare the two named things
points.text: Compare exactly the two things named in the question. Write about both of them. Do not answer about something else that just shares a keyword.

cites.quote: some candidates either only focussed on one of the two methods, or did not discuss the impact of each method on the quality of a video file.

question.quote: Compare the use of static and dynamic routing when sending data packets through IP networks. You must include similarities and differences.

strong.sentence: Both static and dynamic routing are used in routers to decide the next hop that a data packet is sent to.

earns.quote: Used in routers/routing devices to determine next node/router/device/hop to send data packet/datagram/frame

strong.sentence: Both types of routing provide a default route for a packet if no other route can be found.

earns.quote: Both provide default route for packet if no route can be determined

strong.sentence: Network administrators create static routing tables, whereas algorithms create dynamic routing tables.

earns.quote: Static routing tables created by network administrators whereas dynamic routing tables are created by algorithms

strong.sentence: Static routes are fixed, whereas dynamic routing lets packets take different routes depending on network conditions.

earns.quote: Static routes are fixed whereas dynamic routing allows packets to take different routes depending on network conditions

strong.sentence: Static routing tables stay the same when network conditions or devices change, whereas dynamic routing tables update to match the changes.

earns.quote: Static routing tables not updated/amended when network conditions/device change whereas dynamic routing are updated/can adjust to changing network conditions

strong.sentence: Static route information does not time out, whereas dynamic routes have a time-to-live.

earns.quote: Static routing table/info does not ‘time out’ whereas dynamic routes can be time-limited/have time-to-live data

weak.answer: Static IP addresses are set by the network administrator and do not change. Dynamic IP addresses are given out by a DHCP server and can change each time a device connects.
weak.why: It answers about IP addresses, but the question is about routing. It has no similarity. It also describes each type on its own, with no comparison.

basis.quote: It was noted that a significant number of responses referred to dynamic IP assignment using DHCP. Such references did not answer the question and it can only be assumed that the candidates spotted the words ’dynamic’ and ‘IP’ and misunderstood the question.

question.quote: Contrast the characteristics of local area networks (LANs) and wide area networks (WANs).

strong.sentence: A LAN covers a smaller geographical area than a WAN.

earns.quote: LAN covers a smaller geographical area/valid examples than WAN

strong.sentence: A LAN has a higher data transfer speed than a WAN.

earns.quote: LAN has higher data transfer speed/greater bandwidth than WAN

strong.sentence: One organisation usually owns a LAN, whereas a number of organisations often own a WAN.

earns.quote: LANs are (usually) owned by one organisation whereas WANs are (usually/often) owned by a number/collective ownership

strong.sentence: LANs have fewer data transmission errors than WANs.

earns.quote: LANs have fewer data transmission errors than WANs

strong.sentence: LANs have fewer network congestion problems than WANs.

earns.quote: LANs have fewer network congestion problems than WANs

strong.sentence: A LAN uses Layer 1 or 2 devices such as switches and hubs, whereas a WAN uses Layer 3 devices such as routers.

earns.quote: LANs use Layer 1or 2 devices/switches/bridges/hubs/repeaters whereas WANs use Layer 3 devices/Routers/Multi-layer Switches

weak.answer:
• LAN: small area, one building.
• WAN: large area, the internet.
• Both are networks that connect computers.
weak.why: Each bullet states facts about one network. None of them gives a difference. The last bullet is a similarity, and Contrast gives no credit for similarities.

basis.quote: Weaker answers just stated facts, sometimes as unconnected bullets, or described uses of LANs/WANs. Others gave similarities. These did not gain credit because the responses did not answer the question.

thin_evidence: Compare: 16 question parts from 2022 to 2025, all 16 with mark schemes. Contrast: 6 parts from 2022 to 2026, 5 with mark schemes. The sixth part, March 2026 Paper 12 Q7(b), has no mark scheme in the source set. November 2024 Paper 33 Q3(b) is left out. There, 'contrast' is an image term in a Describe question. The examiner reports disagree on whether Compare needs both sides when the question does not ask for both.
